Effective-date reliability is now a Layer 1 prerequisite. Downloaded historical Teams VTTs may have file modification times equal to download/acquisition rather than meeting occurrence; the observed July 10/13 standups exposed the gap. Planned remediation: trustworthy occurrence candidate selection before ID/provider-request minting, explicit --meeting-date override, controlled date repair, and warnings for modification-time fallback.

Roadmap (post-layer1): make meeting-ingest init help consuming repos wire iQ Context. Today init only scaffolds meetings dirs/toml/cache-gitignore/ledger. Proposal: when init detects .iq-context/ in the target root, print a hint to add the meeting artifact globs to .iq-context/config.yaml (or run iq-context init, which auto-detects them), and point at the Post-Ingest Capture protocol. Keep coupling loose: iq-context owns detection/doctor; meeting-ingest init just nudges. Note: capture protocol already travels machine-wide via ~/.claude/skills/meeting-ingest and ~/.codex/skills/meeting-ingest (both updated 2026-07-18); the skill may need a fallback line for repos without iq-context initialized.

UAT feedback from first external consumer run (HTV-IQ-DataAnalytics, Codex agent, 2026-07-18): engine contract held perfectly (no partial side effects across 4 failed phase-2 attempts, safe retries, mtime warning surfaced, capture protocol ran), but the session extractor had to guess the response envelope schema and discover it one validation rejection at a time (owner_related_party, stakeholder_name, then stakeholder+stakeholder_name both), eventually grepping schema.py in the meeting-ingest source repo from the consumer project. Also observed: low-confidence mtime date was noted but baked into meeting ID mtg-20260718-aa2fd13f with no escalation step; two stale handoffs re-reported with no cleanup command; slug truncated mid-word at 80 chars. Prioritized remediation: (1) ship the exact response contract with the phase-1 request payload or skill doc - filled example or JSON schema, not just a contract version string; (2) aggregate all provider-response validation errors in one report instead of fail-fast, plus optional validate-response pre-flight command; (3) skill protocol step: on date_confidence low at phase 1, confirm occurrence date and re-run with --meeting-date before minting. Backlog evidence: stale-handoff cleanup command, word-boundary slug truncation.

body: Dogfood: first Claude Code ingest of 2026-07-20 from HTV-IQ-DataAnalytics processed Migration Planning Sync successfully via the session provider. Manual occurrence-date confirmation converted low-confidence mtime dating to explicit manual confidence; engine produced markdown, 7 signals, archive, completed reconcile, and iQ capture, leaving inbox clean. Friction observed: provider-request and validate/ingest source paths behaved inconsistently and required absolute paths; the dedicated extraction agent consumed 107.2k tokens for one meeting; initial low-confidence request was superseded rather than reused; session-inbox reported stale handoffs that required manual investigation and deletion, including two artifacts for an already-completed meeting and one superseded request. These are concrete Just Works Continuity/readiness and cleanup UX inputs.

Dogfood semantic review for HTV-IQ-DataAnalytics meeting mtg-20260720-cf7f049d, Migration Planning Sync (2026-07-20): summary accurate; decisions accurate; actions correctly attributed and framed; signals strong; owner would use without editing and found the distillation valuable despite a long discussion with interleaved thought streams. One identity defect: generated artifact changed Baba's raw VTT label from 'Opeyemi, Baba' to 'Opeyemi, Baba (Contractor)'. Baba is a client-side employee, not a contractor. Inspection shows this is not a colleague-vs-client engine classification: the current Attendee schema carries display_name, raw_labels, role_context, and confidence only, and the renderer prints provider output directly. The source VTT labels Ken and Jean Francois as '(Contractor)' but not Baba, so the session extraction provider invented/copied the suffix; the wrong label also propagated into two durable signal records. This suggests validation should enforce attendee raw_labels and signal evidence speakers against normalized transcript labels rather than trusting provider-synthesized identity text.

Independent semantic audit of HTV-IQ-DataAnalytics meeting mtg-20260720-cf7f049d found the artifact largely faithful but confirmed four additional framing defects beyond Baba's fabricated Contractor suffix. (1) The Decentrix timing dependency is ~10:06 PM/the last run of the night, not 10:06 AM; AM is repeated in TLDR, T5, R3, and Q5 and Q5 is internally inconsistent with its 9:58 PM alternative. (2) 'Jim' was merged with attendee Jean Francois Harden at high confidence, but the call repeatedly says they still need to ask/message Jim and Ken had not talked to him that morning, suggesting Jim may be a separate non-attendee notebook owner; identity should remain unresolved/low-confidence unless corroborated. (3) TLDR says session exhaustion was 'traced to' transient commit conflicts, overstating causality; the transcript and artifact body explicitly leave root cause unresolved and consider Fabric/session behavior. (4) A5 presents moving Hetal toward a for-loop pattern as an agreed action, but Jean Francois proposed it and Ken/Baba immediately called it untenable/not possible; the actual action was reducing cadence and moving validation toward UAT. Verified all four directly against the artifact and archived VTT. Overall semantic output remains strong, with deterministic facts/identity grounding and proposal-vs-agreement classification as clear validation opportunities.

Approved Runtime dogfood diagnosis for HTV-IQ-DataAnalytics (2026-07-20): two executable installations exist. Global /Users/kmgdev/.local/bin/meeting-ingest is a frozen uv-tool package whose tracked meeting_ingest Python files exactly match main commit 3bc917de8c6072239848ed190c4c45889d6cf227, but metadata exposes only version 0.1.0 and direct_url=file:///Users/kmgdev/dev_projects/meeting-ingest, with no immutable commit identity; post-main hooks can replace it. The maintained Claude skill runs 'uv run meeting-ingest'; from HTV this resolves the local .venv executable and therefore live working-tree code, currently including uncommitted cli.py and playbook.py changes. Before release-quality dogfood, implement Track 1 build identity/readiness/pin enforcement, select an immutable packaged build, update the skill away from ambiguous uv-run resolution, then remove the editable HTV package after explicit approval. Exploratory dev dogfood may continue only if explicitly labeled development evidence with path, module, commit, and dirty state recorded.

body: Engine asymmetry found during Task 5 (not changed, src out of scope): pin_runtime resolves workflow files from <root>/.claude (runtime_release.py:632-633) while inspect_runtime resolves from ~/.claude (runtime.py:638-639). Pinning a fresh consumer root requires project-level .claude copies to exist first, and pin-recorded hashes come from project-level copies while readiness re-hashes user-level ones. The Task 5 acceptance doc works around it by running scripts/install-approved-skill.py against the acceptance root before pinning (matches README shadow-copy step). Open question: intentional or latent bug?

RELAY-BACK from iq-context/trustworthy-state-engine (source: cap_20260726T162156Z_19921e1e routing, unit D commit ad4feb4): the dated-status question this project routed to the iq-context repo is answered and implemented. The obligations parser now classifies status cells by LEADING TOKEN — 'met 2026-07-24 (doc 09)' counts as met/closed; a cell beginning 'open' stays open regardless of later words. Landed on iq-context main (commit ad4feb4, 200/200 tests) 2026-07-26; ships in the next published release. Effect here: the open question 'Whether iq-context should prefix-match dated statuses' can CLOSE at the next session, and after the next iq-context release installs, board-log status cells may carry dates again (the 6270818 normalization workaround is no longer required going forward — no need to revert it).

Owner dogfood feedback (2026-07-26, verbatim substance): the explicit-update/receipt-ceremony model is not user-friendly — 'I'm not looking to use a tool that creates an obligation for me to run a terminal command and continue to make sure I'm up to date… I don't know why the onus is on the consumer to prove what version they are running. They just want it to work.' Owner prefers the npm model: as the tool evolves, all consumers are updated. This contradicts record 002 ratified clauses (explicit update actions; channel never installs/selects/repins) — charter convening trigger met (dogfooding exposed a usability gap). Proposed board brief: segment update policy by consumer class — client-work consumers (HTV) keep fail-closed pins and explicit updates; general consumers get auto-updating distribution with attestation verification running invisibly inside the updater. Cheaper alternative considered: direct owner ruling without the board; insufficient because it reverses a ratified clause and sets external-user trust posture.

NEW FINDINGS from this run:
1. Date gate friction is now 2-for-2. Both HTV runs inferred a low-confidence date from file mtime, forcing abandon-and-remint with --meeting-date. This run also hit 'pending handoff blocks reminting' and needed two extra status/abandon commands to resolve the pair. This is ceremony of exactly the kind the owner objected to in cap_20260727T024600Z. Cheapest fix is skill-level, not engine-level: have the meeting-ingest skill ask the owner for the meeting date before the first mint when the source carries no reliable date signal, instead of minting blind and discovering low confidence afterward.
2. Decisions status vocabulary is an unconstrained contract gap. artifact-contract.md line 808 enumerates open/done/deferred/unknown for Commitments but the Decisions section (lines 777-791) states no vocabulary. This artifact invented three forms in one run: 'decided and implemented' (D1), 'decided' (D2, D3). Stakeholder Asks and Dependencies also append free-text after the leading token ('open — Kushali plans to raise it today', 'open — fix designed, implementation and testing pending'), which satisfies the prefix rule but leaves status columns as prose rather than enumerable values. Bears on downstream playbook/briefing derivation.
3. Signal-sensitivity policy question (owner ruling needed, possible board matter). sig-475b45a1d63f (risk_or_concern, high confidence) and R5 persist a named non-owner colleague's morale/capacity state into a durable client-work artifact that feeds signal JSONL, playbook derivation, and briefings. The rendering softened the verbatim appropriately ('drained by the rework' vs the much stronger and profane original at 05:19), but the question is whether morale language about a named third party belongs in the durable signal stream at all, not whether it was softened well.
4. Per-run model attestation is indirect, not absent. model_id is the constant 'claude-code-session' and model_alias 'balanced' is a quality tier (SUPPORTED_QUALITIES fast/balanced/deep), so the Decision 33 Opus 5 pin for meeting-extraction is attested only through build_id -> receipt -> agent doc frontmatter, not recorded per run. Open question: whether the artifact can evidence that the harness actually honored the subagent pin at run time, given a documented model-fallback regime exists.
5. Version question reinforced. The owner has now seen 'generated_by: meeting-ingest 0.1.0' in a second consecutive artifact header; runtime_provenance semantic_version is likewise 0.1.0 with builds distinguished only by g51ff17173bea.
6. Minor render noise, cleaned-verbatim policy: the transcript opens with a stray non-speech fragment ('Graham, Ken (Contractor) (00:03): description.') and preserves a clear mis-transcription ('He deleted detail and summary' for 'you deleted') — arguably correct under verbatim policy, but the leading fragment is noise rather than speech.
